title: Happy birthday Chiyaan Vikram: Do you know what his real name is?
summary: Tamil actor Chiyaan Vikram, born Kennedy John Victor, celebrates another birthday as fans hail his three-decade career. Known for intense performances, physical transformations and challenging roles, Vikram rose to fame with Bala's Sethu (1999) and cemented his persona with films such as Pithamagan, Anniyan, Raavanan, Deiva Thirumagal, I and Mahaan. His sobriquet 'Chiyaan' came from the iconic Saamy character Aarusaamy in 2003.
content:
Tamil actor Chiyaan Vikram turns a year older today and his fans are celebrating the big day in the biggest possible way. Chiyaan’s original name is Kennedy John Victor. He is popularly known by his stage name Chiyaan Vikram, is an actor, playback singer and producer, prominently known for his work in Tamil cinema.

Vikram, who is known for his spontaneous performances, body transformations, and selection of difficult roles, has made a distinct fame over the years. He’s been doing that for over three decades, and he’s still out here blowing minds and winning the praise of both critics and the public.

Early Career and Breakthrough

Vikram got his start in the early 1990s with minor appearances in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam movies. But his breakthrough film also came in 1999 with Bala’s Sethu. His metamorphosis for the part — both physically and emotionally — earned him rave reviews and created a new trajectory for his career.

Why He’s Called 'Chiyaan'

Vikram's name had become attached to the title Chiyaan after his character in the film Saamy where he portrayed a serious no-nonsense police officer named Aarusaamy back in 2003. He was called 'Chiyaan Vikram' and that name stayed ever since; the character was so iconic.

Some of Chiyaan Vikram’s Best Films

Sethu (1999)
Director: Bala
Why To Watch: A tragic tale of love that saw Vikram lose a lot of weight and impersonate a man with serious mental problems. It’s the movie that changed his career.

Pithamagan (2003)
Director: Bala
Why Watch: Vikram was burdened with a tough role; this time he played a grave-digger who couldn’t speak regularly. He won the National Film Award for Best Actor for his wordless, haunting passage.

Anniyan (2005)
Director: Shankar
Why Watch: A psychological thriller where Vikram plays a man with multiple personality disorder. From a meek lawyer to a violent vigilante, his layered performance was widely praised.

Raavanan (2010)
Director: Mani Ratnam
Why Watch: A Tamil adaptation of the Ramayana from the villain’s perspective. Vikram portrayed Veera, a complex anti-hero with emotion and raw power.

Deiva Thirumagal (2011)
Director: A. L. Vijay
Why Watch: Vikram’s performance as a mentally challenged father in a custody battle was heart-wrenching. It earned him comparisons to the critically acclaimed and emotionally charged film, I Am Sam.

I (2015)
Director: Shankar
Why Watch: Vikram underwent an astonishing transformation from a bodybuilder to a model with facial scars. The film had grand visuals, and Vikram's devotion to the character was jaw-dropping.

Mahaan (2022)
Director: Karthik Subbaraj
Why Watch: A gangster-drama where Vikram stars alongside his real-life son Dhruv Vikram. The film touches on concepts of identity, freedom, rebellion, and family relationships.

The actor's willingness to physically and emotionally reinvent himself for roles, plus his decades-long body of work across Tamil cinema, has kept him relevant and respected. Fans and critics alike often highlight his fearless role choices and his capacity to disappear into characters. You are already a Moneycontrol Pro user.
